title: Leonurine alleviates lung ischemia-reperfusion injury through suppression of ferroptosis via RORalpha in male mice.
authors: Chen, Wanying; Yang, Li; Xue, Yincong; Zhang, Yuting; Chen, Chengshui; Huang, Shuai
one_liner_zh: 研究中药单体LEO通过RORalpha/Nrf2/GPX4轴抑制铁死亡减轻肺缺血再灌注损伤，仅含分子对接且非蛋白-DNA互作，与本课题无关。
abstract: Lung ischemia-reperfusion injury (LIRI) is a complex pathological condition that significantly impairs clinical outcomes following lung transplantation and thoracic surgery. Leonurine (LEO), an alkaloid derived from Leonurus japonicus, which has known anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, has shown therapeutic potential in various oxidative stress-related diseases. However, the effects of LEO on LIRI and its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In the present study, a murine model of LIRI was established using wild-type mice. LEO treatment significantly improved lung histopathology, reduced oxidative stress, decreased pulmonary edema, and enhanced survival. Bioinformatics analyses - including volcano plot, KEGG enrichment, and GSEA - identified ferroptosis as a key regulatory pathway. In vivo and in vitro assays (HE, 4-HNE, and DHE labeling; immunofluorescence; and immunoblotting) confirmed that LEO inhibited ferroptosis in lung tissue and in MLE-12 cells. Mechanistically, LEO upregulated the RORalpha/Nrf2/GPX4 axis, thereby reducing lipid peroxidation and iron overload, as validated by BODIPY581/591 C11 and FeRhoNox-1 staining. Moreover, RORalpha inhibition abolished the anti-ferroptotic effects of LEO, indicating that its protective function is RORalpha dependent. Molecular docking further supported a potential direct interaction between LEO and RORalpha. Collectively, LEO alleviates LIRI by inhibiting ferroptosis through activation of the RORalpha/Nrf2/GPX4 signaling pathway. These findings suggest that LEO may serve as a promising therapeutic agent for the treatment of LIRI.
abstract_zh: 肺缺血再灌注损伤（LIRI）是一种复杂的病理状态，显著影响肺移植和胸外科手术后的临床结局。益母草碱（LEO）是从益母草（Leonurus japonicus）中提取的一种生物碱，具有已知的抗炎和抗氧化特性，在多种氧化应激相关疾病中显示出治疗潜力。然而，LEO对LIRI的作用及其潜在机制仍不清楚。在本研究中，使用野生型小鼠建立了LIRI小鼠模型。LEO治疗显著改善了肺组织病理学，减少了氧化应激，减轻了肺水肿，并提高了生存率。生物信息学分析——包括火山图、KEGG富集和GSEA——将铁死亡（ferroptosis）确定为一个关键调控通路。体内和体外实验（HE、4-HNE和DHE标记；免疫荧光；以及免疫印迹）证实，LEO抑制了肺组织和MLE-12细胞中的铁死亡。机制上，LEO上调了RORalpha/Nrf2/GPX4轴，从而减少了脂质过氧化和铁过载，这通过BODIPY581/591 C11和FeRhoNox-1染色得到验证。此外，RORalpha抑制消除了LEO的抗铁死亡效应，表明其保护功能依赖于RORalpha。分子对接进一步支持LEO与RORalpha之间可能存在直接相互作用。综上，LEO通过激活RORalpha/Nrf2/GPX4信号通路抑制铁死亡，从而缓解LIRI。这些发现表明，LEO可能作为治疗LIRI的一种有前景的治疗药物。
